name: Two-Way Traffic
spec: yellow diamond with two black vertical arrows pointing in opposite directions
meaning: You are entering a road with traffic in both directions.

snippets.back: A two-way traffic sign means you are leaving a separated one-way roadway for a two-way road, and it also reminds drivers they are on a two-way road.

Yellow warnings preview wet slipperiness, merging traffic, divided-highway shifts, two-way traffic, ending lanes, signals ahead, crossings, added lanes, crossroads, stop or yield ahead, curves, windings.

Warning signs alert drivers to two-way traffic ahead, merging traffic, right-lane reductions, upcoming roundabouts, divided highways ahead, and divided highway ends—where the divided roadway ends three hundred fifty to five hundred feet ahead before two-way traffic resumes.
A divided-highway-begins sign means two-way traffic is about to split around a center strip.
A Two-Way Traffic sign warns that a divided multilane highway changes to a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions.
After leaving the interstate, be alert for a change to two-way traffic.
A warning with opposing vertical arrows indicates two-way traffic.
Opposing vertical arrows on a yellow diamond warn of two-way traffic.

result.summary: Official snippets state the sign means leaving a separated roadway for two-way traffic and warn of opposing vertical arrows on a yellow diamond.
